### Observed differences

- The clearest difference is a flip between two alternative three-activity groups in the stage after A19 and A20. In the earlier window, A21, A22 and A23 each ran in about 75 in 100 traces (typically together, in no fixed order), while A24, A25 and A26 each ran in about 25 in 100; in the later window this reversed — A21–A23 each ran in about 25 in 100 traces and A24–A26 each in about 75–77 in 100. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]
- A20's outgoing transitions flipped accordingly: earlier, about 27%, 23% and 26% went to A21, A22 and A23 and about 25% to A24–A26 combined; later, about 25%, 22% and 28% went to A24, A25 and A26 and about 24% to A21–A23. A19 shows the same relational flip and still precedes whichever group runs. [DIR002, REL013, REL016, REL019, REL022]
- The two groups remain mutually exclusive alternatives in both windows (A21 and A24 together in about 0.5 in 100 traces earlier, 2 in 100 later), and each still executes as a block: A24 with A25 co-occur in about 25 in 100 traces earlier versus 76 in 100 later; A21 with A22 in about 75 in 100 earlier versus 25 in 100 later. [REL027, REL049, REL025]
- A06 became both more frequent and differently placed: it ran in about 17 in 100 traces earlier versus about 53 in 100 later, its median event position moved from mid-trace (about 0.48) to near the end (0.96), and its outgoing transitions went from spread over many activities (largest share about 21% to A33) to about 90% to A35, with A35 following within one step in about 97 in 100 of the later observed pairs. It now also co-occurs with A19/A20/A29/A30 in about 52 in 100 traces (they precede it) versus 17 in 100 earlier. [OCC002, POS001, DIR001, LAG001, REL001, REL009]
- A34's hand-over changed: earlier about 89% of its outgoing transitions went straight to A35 (one step apart in about 90 in 100 traces); later about 50% go to A06 and 48% to A35, and A34 and A35 are two steps apart in about half the traces — consistent with A06 sitting between them in roughly half of the later cases. [DIR005, LAG013, REL011, REL012]
- A02 and A08 became rarer: participation fell from about 17 to 8 in 100 traces (A02) and from about 14 to 5 (A08). [OCC001, OCC003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the share of cases taking the A21–A23 branch after A19 and A20 fell from about 75 in 100 to about 25 in 100, while the alternative A24–A26 branch rose from about 25 in 100 to about 75 in 100. The flip is visible directly in A20's outgoing distribution and consistently in the participation of all six activities and their co-occurrence with A19 and A20, whose order before the active group is preserved; both branches are observed substantially in both windows and remain mutually exclusive, so this is a change in how often existing paths are taken rather than a replacement of one path by another. The volume of qualifying items (92 versus about 1 expected for an unchanged process) makes chance sampling unlikely as an overall explanation. What the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows draw on different case mixes rather than a changed routing rule, and the outgoing-transition shares at A20 are not case-level probabilities. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, DIR002, REL013, REL016, REL019, REL022, REL025, REL027, REL049, REL055]

Other differences: A06 shows a distinct, well-supported placement change — it occurs in about 53 in 100 later traces (versus 17 in 100 earlier), sits near the end of the trace, and in roughly half of the later cases is inserted between A34 and A35 (A34 now leads to A06 about half the time, and A06 is followed by A35 within one step in about 97 in 100 of the later pairs), where earlier A34 led almost directly to A35. [OCC002, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, LAG001, LAG013, REL011, REL012] Separately, A02 and A08 participation decreased. [OCC001, OCC003]
